text: These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the surviving elders of the exile, and to the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jehoiachin, the queen mother, the court officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and metalworkers had gone out from Jerusalem.
He sent it by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in Babylon. It said:
This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles whom I carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon:

versions.text: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon:
versions.explanation: Here the verb is הגליתי ("carried into exile"), while verse 20 uses שלחתי ("sent"). Rendering both as "sent away" blurs a distinction the Hebrew makes and weakens the force of the exile language.

text: Build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Take wives and have sons and daughters; find wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so that they too may have sons and daughters. Multiply there; do not dwindle away.
Seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.
For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Do not let your prophets among you or your diviners deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you encourage them to dream.

versions.text: For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Do not let the prophets among you or your diviners deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams you make them dream.
versions.explanation: Two small improvements: the Hebrew has "your prophets who are among you" (possessive), and "the dreams you make them dream" leaves "them" with an unclear antecedent when read aloud; "that you encourage them to dream" clarifies the causative sense of מַחְלְמִים.

text: They are prophesying lies to you in my name. I did not send them, declares the LORD.
For this is what the LORD says: When Babylon's seventy years are complete, I will attend to you and fulfill my good promise to you, to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans I have for you, declares the LORD—plans for peace and not for harm, to give you a future and a hope.
Then you will call on me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.

versions.text: Then you will call on me and come to me, and I will listen to you.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has three verbs: קרא (call), הלך (come/go), and התפלל (pray). The verb "pray" has been dropped, losing content that is central to the verse's meaning.

text: You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.

I will let myself be found by you, declares the LORD, and I will restore your fortunes. I will gather you from all the nations and all the places where I have driven you, declares the LORD, and I will bring you back to the place from which I sent you into exile.
But you say, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon."
This is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne and about all the people who remain in this city, your brothers who did not go with you into exile—
this is what the LORD of hosts says: I am sending sword, famine, and plague against them, and I will make them like rotten figs, too bad to be eaten.

I will pursue them with sword, famine, and plague, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth—a curse, a desolation, an object of scorn and reproach among all the nations where I have driven them.
For they did not listen to my words, declares the LORD, which I sent to them again and again by my servants the prophets—and you did not listen either, declares the LORD.
So hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in my name: I am handing them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will put them to death before your eyes.
Because of them this curse will be used by all the exiles of Judah in Babylon: "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in the fire."

For they have done an outrageous thing in Israel: they committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and spoke lying words in my name, which I did not command them. I am the one who knows, and I am witness, declares the LORD.
To Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall say this:

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You have sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

"The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be the officer in charge of the house of the LORD, over every madman who plays the prophet, so that you should put him in the stocks and in irons.
So why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who keeps playing the prophet among you?
For he has even sent word to us in Babylon: 'It will be a long time. Build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat their fruit.'"
Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
Send word to all the exiles: This is what the LORD says concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you when I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie,

Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will have no one left living among this people, nor will he see the good I am going to do for my people, declares the LORD, because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.

versions.text: therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will have no one left among this people, nor will he see the good I am going to do for my people, declares the LORD, because he has preached rebellion against the LORD.
versions.explanation: Two small refinements: the Hebrew has 'a man dwelling/living among this people,' so adding 'living' captures the participle יוֹשֵׁב and clarifies the sense; and דִּבֶּר is simply 'spoken,' so 'spoken rebellion' is more literal than the interpretive 'preached.' The opening 'Therefore' also reads better capitalized as the start of a new sentence in oral reading.
